div.div:
Run lifecycle
① Sign in (Cognito), describe a goal
② Planner drafts a task graph (async)
③ Review, edit, save as a versioned workflow
④ Run now, or attach a rate / cron schedule
⑤ Interpreter executes waves; workers fan out in parallel and call tools via the Gateway
⑥ Outputs land in S3; status & tokens on the run record
⑦ Report harness assembles the final artifact, noting gaps
⑧ Browse runs & artifacts (presigned reads)

text.tspan: ① Sign in (Cognito), describe a goal
② Planner drafts a task graph (async)
③ Review, edit, save as a versioned
④ Run now, or attach a rate / cron schedule
⑤ Interpreter executes waves; workers fan
out in parallel and call tools via the Gateway
⑥ Outputs land in S3; status & tokens on
⑦ Report harness assembles the final

div.div:
How a plan executes
One generic state machine runs any valid plan:
PrepareRun → per wave (sequential) → Map over tasks (parallel) → invokeHarness → PersistArtifact → EvaluateRunHealth → report → FinalizeRun
Failure policies: contain (default) · fail-fast · retry-run. Failed tasks are recorded, dependents are skipped with a reason, and the report declares the gaps.

text.tspan: One generic state machine runs any valid plan:
PrepareRun → per wave (sequential) → Map over tasks
Failure policies: contain (default) · fail-fast · retry-run. Failed
tasks are recorded, dependents are skipped with a reason,
and the report declares the gaps.

div.div: Least-privilege IAM per harness and per tool Lambda · runtime roles carry no control-plane permissions (the only resource ever created at runtime is a per-workflow EventBridge schedule; everything else exists only via CDK) · KMS encryption on artifacts, tables and logs · secrets never exposed to agents · cost-attribution tags (workload / component / env) on every resource · token usage captured on every run record
